title: Why Is the Sky Blue but Sunsets Red?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why is the sky blue, but the sunset red?
Same sun, same air. Only the path through the air changes.
Sunlight is every colour mixed together.
Air molecules knock some of it sideways, and they scatter blue about six times more strongly than red.
That scattered blue reaches you from every direction. That's the blue sky.
At sunset, the light skims in almost flat, through about thirty-eight times more air.
Even in clean air, less than a thousandth of the blue survives that trip. About a quarter of the red does.
So the sun glows orange and red.
And the blue you lost? Somebody to the west gets it, as their afternoon sky.
